eligibility.reason: E1/E4: a running talker and a five-second backwards system-clock step reproduce the pause. E2 reaches step 6: rcl computes a timer timeout and rmw_fastrtps waits against a different clock domain; changing the peer behavior changes the failure. E3: PAIR across rmw_wait. The fix history also changes the declared rmw_wait timing contract, so this is not merely deployment naming or a build-only defect.
eligibility.quote: However, condition_variable->wait_for eventually executes futex system call that uses the system clock and can be affected by the system's time adjustment.

failed_conditions.quote: if `rmw_wait` uses the system clock, a rcl timer using steady time isn't going to work fine (issue happens when system time is adjusted backwards)...
failed_conditions.reason: The shared timeout has inconsistent clock semantics across rcl/rmw_fastrtps. No listed specific class names that mismatch; other and api:rmw_wait are appropriate. A missed timer invocation is an effect, not independent proof of a requested publisher-rate contract.

loudness.quote: Timer callback execution waits 5 seconds when the system timer is adjusted to backward.
loudness.reason: The report shows ordinary publishing logs and an observed timing discontinuity, with no early diagnostic of the clock mismatch.

detection_stage.quote: Adjust system time manually in another terminal.
detection_stage.reason: The reproducer changes time while the talker is already running.

resolution.quote: I have confirmed that the bug is fixed in the following environments.
resolution.reason: The confirmation names Ubuntu22.04, rolling, rmw_fastrtps_cpp and a nightly image digest, not both specified unit revisions. It establishes an environment-level successful fix but not observed status under S1's stricter two-revision criterion; recommended remains appropriate.

notes: The compiler/libstdc++ change supplies the runtime behavior fix, while rmw PR #316 updates the declared clock expectation. Do not claim the documentation edit alone removes the pause. The cited discussion also considers system-time and accelerated ROS-time timers; those are not additional reproduced failures in this steady-timer composition. The quoted comment fragment #issuecomment-763000000 was opened and is valid.
